rationale: This is a pure factorial recombination of two archive signals (SelfFundedExpanderRegime's sign gate with FullNetDistributionGatedExpansion's surplus definition) with no new economic content, and since the classifier is bounded at ±1 essentially all cross-sectional dispersion comes from the asset-growth magnitude leg — i.e. the signal is largely a sign-conditioned asset-growth anomaly, which the archive's PureExpanderFundingRegime result (fmb +3.82 but ls_alpha −0.033) already warns about.

Another one-lever swap in the same 2x2 (surprise-scaled deployment already tested at 5.3%/t=3.71 with the continuous full-net gate; the sign gate already tested with gross flows), and it inherits the same problem that a ±1 gate leaves the deployment surprise doing all the ranking work, so the incremental information over its two parents is minimal.

The clearest practical motivation of the six — pairing the within-firm deployment surprise with the balance-sheet reconstruction of internal funds addresses the family's binding coverage constraint rather than reshuffling gate forms — though the 5-year MA on asset growth will claw back part of the promised 0.126 coverage and the construction remains an incremental variant of two well-tested archive components.

Identical to MarginTrajectoryAndFundingExpansion except the surplus term is redefined from gross to net flows — a single-term substitution whose expected effect (a modest shift in one of two equally ranked composite legs) is too small to constitute a substantively different hypothesis.

A cosmetic swap of the surplus definition inside the already-tested DilutionAwareFundingExpansion, and the two legs now partially offset rather than complement — the full-net surplus rewards repurchases while the csho-growth rank penalizes issuance, so both legs load on the same net-equity-issuance dimension that the share-issuance anomaly literature already spans.

Internally inconsistent with its own stated design — the nested SUMRANK gives the cash-surplus leg roughly double the weight of slack and dilution rather than the claimed "equally weighted ranks" — and the NEG(lt/at) leg imports a plain low-leverage/quality tilt that risks driving any measured alpha independently of the funding mechanism.
